_comment: Credentials for the mobile-app link association files served from
/.well-known/ (see scripts/emit-well-known.mjs).
These are the only values that stand between a shared link and the app
opening it: Android will not hand indigenworld.com/post/<id> to the app
until it has fetched assetlinks.json and matched the signing certificate
of the installed build against a fingerprint listed below.
Nothing here is a secret. A signing certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint is
public by design — it is what every device checks the association with —
and so is an Apple team id.
HOW TO FILL android.sha256CertFingerprints:
Every key that can sign a build members install must be listed, or
links break for whoever has the build signed by the missing key.
- Play App Signing (the one that matters for the Play install):
Play Console > your app > Test and release > Setup > App signing >
'App signing key certificate' > SHA-256 certificate fingerprint.
- Any local release key, and the upload key:
cd apps/mobile/android && ./gradlew :app:signingReport
Paste them uppercase, colon-separated, exactly as reported.
HOW TO FILL apple.appIds:
'<TEAM ID>.world.indigen.mobile'. The team id is in the Apple Developer
account under Membership details. Leave the list empty until the iOS
build actually declares the associated-domains entitlement — an
apple-app-site-association naming an app that does not claim the domain
is worse than none at all.
The hosts these files vouch for are wherever they are served from, which
is indigenworld.com and www.indigenworld.com. They are not configured
here; the Android manifest names them in its App Links filter.
An empty list means the file is not generated and not deployed, which is
deliberate: a malformed or wrong association file makes Android cache a
verification failure, and no link opens the app until the cache expires.
